chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from one of our companions from Aban ibn Uthman from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Sari from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he asked him
about the man looking at the woman before he marries her. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, so why is he giving his wealth'.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a man to look at a woman before marriage in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the permissibility of pre-marital viewing (*al-nazar*) by linking it to the rationale of the dowry (*mahr*); if the purpose of financial exchange is to secure a spouse, the right to inspect her is inherent. This ruling is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for validating the consent and compatibility checks before the *Ijab* and *Qabul* (offer and acceptance) are finalized. It underscores that viewing is not merely a cultural courtesy but a juristic right derived from the logic of the marriage contract itself.
